title: Search URL Common Prefix
real_world_story: In search engine result breadcrumbs and site clustering, web crawlers group related URLs under a unified site hierarchy prefix (such as 'https://example.com/docs/api/'). Determining the longest common prefix among a cluster of grouped URLs allows the search frontend to collapse redundant prefixes and render clean navigational breadcrumbs.
problem_statement: Given an array of N search URL path strings, find the longest common prefix shared by all N strings. A common prefix is a substring that occurs at the beginning of every string in the collection. If there is no common prefix (or if the strings share no common first character), print EMPTY.
task: Compute and print the longest common prefix among the N URL path strings, or EMPTY.
input_format:
The first line contains an integer N, the number of URL strings.
The next N lines each contain a non-empty string.
output_format: Print the longest common prefix string. If no common prefix exists, print EMPTY.

examples.explanation: All three URL strings share the initial prefix 'api/v1/users/'.
The strings start with 's', 'd', and 'h' respectively. There is no shared prefix, so output EMPTY.

real_world_takeaway: Longest Common Prefix extraction enables URL routing compression and cleaner hierarchy abstraction in web navigation and search result pages.
